newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares slide 2.13 pct on political anxiety.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares slide 2.13 pct on political anxiety.

text.p: Shares closed sharply lower on the Delhi Stock Exchange in brisk trade on Thursday as a deepening political crisis triggered panic selling, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 16.02 points, or 2.13 percent, lower at 750.50.

Brokers said the decision of the Congress party to issue a whip to its members in parliament to vote against Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda in a confidence motion on Friday, triggered panic selling on the bourse.
"If the government fails to prove its majority in the house tomorrow the fate of the financial bill and budget will be in the dark," said Arvind Sukumar of brokers Zair Financial Consultants.
The budget, now before parliament, has been held hostage to the political crisis since Congress withdrew its support to Deve Gowda on March 30, jolting the financial markets.
"If the budget is not passed then that would pull back the share prices which had picked up in the post-budget trading sessions," Sukumar added.
Indian share prices had increased by more than 10 percent in the period after the fiscal budget 1997/98 (April-March) was announced on February 28.
Parliament's lower house will convene on Friday at 11 a.m. (0530 GMT) to take up the vote of confidence in Deve Gowda.
Reliance Industries fell 7.60 rupees to 266.00 on selling by speculators and financial institutions, brokers said.
State Bank of India dropped 9.40 rupees to 274.55.
